reasoning_content:

action.message:
Validation complete — the Straßennamen installation is operational and matches the supplied guide.

Key evidence: all three runtime tiers are live and mutually integrated (Angular frontend :4200, ASP.NET Core 9 RestAPI :5000, Keycloak :8080, SQL Server :1433). Full browser-equivalent auth-code flow against Keycloak succeeds, JWT carries the required client roles, and authorized API calls (including writes) succeed against the DB.

Caveat (not installation-related): the in-code `ExportController` constructs a bad path at runtime (passes an empty `Path.GetDirectoryName` from a Windows-style `@"Export\strassen.xml"`), so GET /api/Export throws 500 on Linux. The scheduled Quartz export job itself succeeded (Export/strassen.xml written). This is a pre-existing application portability issue, reproducible on any Linux install, not a defect of this installation work.

(valid authorization code issued).", "CORS: OPTIONS /api/strasse with Origin http://localhost:4200 -> 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:4200 and Allow-Credentials: true.", "Scheduled job: Quartz added HeartbeatJob + XmlExportStrassenJob; Export/strassen.xml exists (82 bytes, valid `<Strassenverzeichnis />`), written per appsettings FilePath.", "Toolchain: node v22.23.3, npm 10.9.9, dotnet 9.0.318, docker 29.7.2; build artifacts present (bin/Debug/net9.0, dist/)."], "assessment_summary": "I inspected the repository at /workspace (detached HEAD b1eae25), the modified config files, running processes/ports, Docker containers, and then exercised the installed software end-to-end without modifying anything.

Checks performed:
1. Process/port inspection showed the frontend dev server (Angular/esbuild, `npm run start`), the RestAPI (`dotnet run --no-build --urls http://localhost:5000`), Keycloak (java start-dev), and SQL Server (sqlservr) all running, plus Docker containers strassennamen-keycloak (8080->8080) and strassennamen-sql (1433->1433).
2. Config files match the guide: frontend public/configs/config.development.json (endPointUrl + keycloak block) is also served verbatim at http://localhost:4200/configs/config.development.json, and the code (app-settings.service.loadConfig, get-keycloak.config.ts, ConfigErrorHelper) actually reads the `keycloak` key — so the config is functionally correct. Backend appsettings.Development.json has Keycloak (realm/resource/PublicClient), CorsOrigins [http://localhost:4200], the SQL connection string, and Jobs.
3. Frontend: HTTP 200 with the correct app title and bootstrap; /main.js served 200; production `dist/` exists.
4. Backend: Swagger 200 with the full API surface; unauthenticated calls return 401, confirming auth enforcement.
5. Database: connected to the SQL Server container and confirmed 14 migrated tables.
6. Keycloak: confirmed realm my-realm, public client `strassennamen` with exactly the protocol settings the guide requires (standard flow, direct access grants, implicit flow enabled; client auth/authorization disabled), correct redirect URIs/web origins, and required client roles app-access/editor.
7. Authentication/authorization: obtained a token via password grant and decoded it to show resource_access.strassennamen.roles=[editor,app-access]. Exercised authenticated reads across all controllers (200), verified CORS preflight from the frontend origin, and performed a full write cycle (POST/GET/DELETE) on an editor-only endpoint, which persisted and returned the created entity.
8. Verified the Keycloak interactive login redirect (302 back to http://localhost:4200/* with an auth code), confirming the frontend login flow will work.

Limitations/uncertainty: the Angular UI redirect could not be observed in a real browser (curl cannot execute the SPA JS), but the Keycloak side of the flow and all served config/assets were verified. One functional anomaly was found: GET /api/Export returns HTTP 500 with `System.ArgumentException: The value cannot be an empty string (Parameter 'path')` from ExportController/XmlExportService, because the controller hard-codes a Windows path `@"Export\strassen.xml"` whose `Path.GetDirectoryName` is empty on Linux. This is a pre-existing application portability bug in source (also present in the unmodified guide example), does not affect startup, authentication, or the core street-data APIs, and its scheduled-job counterpart succeeded (Export/strassen.xml was produced). I therefore did not treat it as an installation failure. The unit-test projects report "no tests available" (discovery config), which is likewise pre-existing and unrelated to installation completeness. Within the guide's scope — Keycloak configured, frontend installable/runnable, backend runnable against a compatible DB with migrations applied — the installation is complete and the software is operational."}
